property_summary: For any nonzero msg.value sent to go(), contract C always forwards its full remaining balance to owner (so address(c).balance == 0 after the call); the mutant that transfers 0 breaks this by leaving a nonzero balance for some inputs.

For any caller and any ETH amount sent to go(), C always ends with zero contract balance (it forwards all received funds to owner); the mutant that transfers 0 can leave a nonzero contract balance for some inputs.

For any caller sending a positive msg.value to go and when the external target call succeeds, the correct contract forwards all remaining balance out so address(c).balance == 0 after go(); the mutant that does payable(owner).transfer(0) can leave a nonzero contract balance for some fuzzed msg.value and target behavior.

For any amount of ETH sent to go() when the external target call succeeds (i.e., does not revert), the reference contract always ends with zero balance (it forwards all funds to owner); the mutant that replaces payable(owner).transfer(address(this).balance) with transfer(0) can leave a nonzero contract balance for some fuzzed msg.value and a cooperating target, breaking this property.

For any caller and any nonzero ETH amount sent to go() when the external callee accepts the forwarded value (does not revert), the reference contract forwards its entire balance out to owner so address(c).balance == 0 after go(); the mutant that replaces payable(owner).transfer(address(this).balance) with transfer(0) can leave a nonzero contract balance, violating this property for some inputs.

For any ETH value sent into C.go when the callee target reverts in its fallback/receive, the reference forwards the received ETH to owner (leaving C balance zero), but the mutant that calls target with value 0 keeps the ETH in C (non-zero balance) for some inputs, breaking the rule.

If an external call to the fixed target address reverts when receiving funds, the reference forwards any msg.value it received to owner (leaving contract balance zero), whereas the mutant that calls the target with value 0 keeps the received funds in the contract (non-zero balance) for some fuzzed msg.value, so for all admissible fuzzed msg.value the reference ensures address(c).balance == 0 after go() when the target reverts, but the mutant can make address(c).balance != 0 for some msg.value.

For any nonzero ether sent to C.go when the external target's fallback reverts, the reference forwards all received ether out so address(c).balance == 0 after the call; the mutant that calls the target with zero value can retain the sent ether, making address(c).balance > 0 for some fuzzed msg.value.

For any caller and any ETH amount sent to C.go, if the callee target's fallback reverts when it receives ETH, the reference contract always ends with zero balance (it forwards received ETH to owner), while the mutant that calls the target with zero value can retain the ETH causing address(c).balance > 0 for some fuzzed amounts and callers.

For any caller and any msg.value >= 0 when the callee (target) reverts on receiving ETH, the correct contract forwards all received ETH to owner leaving address(c).balance == 0 after go(); the mutant that calls the target with value 0 can keep funds so address(c).balance > 0 for some fuzzed msg.value, so the invariant "address(c).balance == 0 after go when target reverts" holds for reference but is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For every call to go() forwarding arbitrary msg.value to the external target that succeeds, the contract C always forwards its remaining balance to its owner (so address(c).balance == 0 and owner still owns funds); the mutant burns the remaining balance to address(0) so address(c).balance == 0 still holds but owner does not receive funds — we assert that owner's balance increases by the sent value (i.e., owner gains the forwarded balance) which holds for the reference and is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For any caller and any ether value sent to go(), after go() returns the contract's owner address balance increases by the amount that was forwarded to the external target (i.e., owner receives the contract's remaining balance); the mutant that transfers balance to address(0) breaks this by leaving the owner unchanged for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero ETH amount forwarded through go() to a potentially reverting external target that accepts the call, the contract C always ends with its owner having a strictly higher balance than before the call (the buggy mutant that sends remaining balance to address(0) can violate this).

For any caller and any ETH amount sent to go(), if the external target accepts the forwarded call (does not revert), then after go() completes the contract's owner address has strictly greater balance than before; the mutant that sends remaining balance to address(0) can violate this for some inputs.

After any successful go() call that forwards msg.value to the target (which may accept funds), the reference contract always pays out its entire remaining balance to owner (leaving address(c).balance == 0), whereas the mutant sometimes leaves half the balance in the contract (address(c).balance != 0) — so the invariant address(c).balance == 0 holds for all inputs on the reference and is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For any caller and any payable amount sent to go(), after go() returns the contract forwards its entire balance to owner (leaving address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that transfers only half the balance can leave a nonzero balance for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any payable amount sent to go() when the external target call succeeds, contract C always ends with zero balance (it forwards all remaining funds to owner); the mutant sending only half can leave a nonzero balance, so the property is: if the external call to target succeeds then address(c).balance == 0 after go() returns.

For any caller and any payable amount, if the call from C.go to its external target reverts (so C keeps the forwarded msg.value), then the reference contract always forwards its entire remaining balance to owner (leaving address(c).balance == 0), while the mutant that transfers only half can leave a non-zero balance; thus: when the external call reverts, address(c).balance == 0 for the reference but may be >0 for the mutant.

For any caller and any payable amount sent to go(), after go() returns the reference C always transfers its entire balance to owner (so owner’s balance increases by exactly the amount sent in), whereas the mutant that transfers only half can make the owner's balance increase by strictly less than the sent amount for some inputs; the test asserts owner’s balance increases by the exact msg.value forwarded to the external target when the external call succeeds.
